Metadata.title: Pool4ward — Design transport as close to reality as possible
Metadata.description: Pool4ward supports companies from transport engineering to contracting: control costs, reduce risks, secure capacity.

Footer.statement: From transport engineering to contracting: control costs, reduce risks, secure capacity.
Footer.demoNote: Cases, sites and values labelled “demonstration” are fictitious. The globe layers are aggregated projections: see the Datasets page.

Capabilities.title: One continuous line, from the first study to the managed contract.
Capabilities.lede: Each capability picks up what the previous one established. You can enter through any of them; you do not have to buy everything to start.

engineering.name: Transport engineering
engineering.question: Which transport organisation does your ground really allow?
engineering.summary: Start from flows, sites, equipment, drivers and energy to compare possible organisations — before talking price.
covers: Flow studies between sites: hubs and cross-docks, shift to rail, inland waterway or sea, loops between sites, regular rounds, long-haul consolidation, electrification of links.
Equipment, driving-time regulation, energy resources (electricity, charging points, diesel) and contracts in force are taken into account.
Each scenario is compared with a baseline built on your own flows.
engineering.scope: Dock windows and service requirements are recorded with you and enter the feasibility analysis; they are not deduced automatically.

tenders.name: Tender preparation
tenders.question: How do you put what you designed out to tender?
tenders.summary: Turn the retained scenario into clear tender lots: flows, geographic meshes, price grids, clauses, ancillary services.
covers: A multi-step preparation assistant: flow selection, lines by postal mesh, zone or region, tiered grids, fuel-revision clause, ancillary services, scenario test.
A tender file in a protected spreadsheet format, with preview, ready to be issued.
Publication of zones and grid templates in CarrierBridge.
tenders.scope: The scope described here is the preparation of the tender file.

carriers.name: Carrier search
carriers.question: Which partners should you approach for each lot?
carriers.summary: Target the operators and carriers whose offer fits the lot — by corridor, mode and equipment — rather than sending the same brief to everyone.
covers: Selection of intermodal operators (rail, inland waterway, sea), ranked by corridor, from the Modal4ward service catalogue.
Matching with the shipper’s current carriers.
A listed carrier is not an available carrier: availability is confirmed by its reply.
carriers.scope: Coverage depends on the datasets: it is shown, by mode and area, on the Datasets page.

comparison.name: Offer comparison
comparison.question: Are the offers you received comparable?
comparison.summary: Bring heterogeneous replies to the same scope, the same volume assumptions and the same conditions before comparing prices.
covers: Reading offers on a common basis: scope covered, volume assumption, price structure, capacity commitment, adjustment conditions.
Highlighting differences in assumptions before any ranking by price.
Arbitration between offers on full cost, service and resources used — not on unit price alone.
comparison.scope: This page describes the method. The precise software functions are shown in a meeting, on your own tenders.

contracts.name: Contract management
contracts.question: What does each contract cover, until when, and what happens to the plan at expiry?
contracts.summary: Attach each contract to the links it covers, its dates and its documents, to know what is committed and when another organisation becomes possible again.
covers: A contract register: code, start and end dates, carrier, attachments, bulk assignment to the links concerned.
Contracts are read in the engineering tool: covered links are flagged, and the end dates of a tender’s contracts are listed.
Commitment terms — capacity, service, duration, adjustment, milestones — are defined with you in the tender brief.
contracts.scope: The scope described here is the contract register, its link to the shipping links, its documents and its deadlines.

Status.label: Five levels of knowledge
Status.lede: We never mix what we have referenced, what we have detected, what we have studied, what a partner has confirmed and what is signed.
